key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces toward stoichiometric composition, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling surface composition and passivator chemistry offers a route to higher-efficiency methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Use neutral ethylenediamine to chelate undercoordinated metals and remove excess surface tin.
Compare this reconstruction with initial passivation and subsequent deprotonation by ethylenediammonium iodide.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term device stability or scalable processing, and passivator evolution depends on surface defects.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
